text:
Ben Carter: pulling DevEx folks in here — we’re tightening the onboarding email CTAs + console checklist this week. Can we list the top “quickstart friction points” we should fix in docs/templates ASAP? Trying to cut time-to-first-success.

Ben Carter: draft notes doc (messy) -> https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1QkS-DevEx-QuickstartFriction (WIP). please add bullets / links.

Henry Cho: from the activation definition debate: we’re optimizing for “first successful production-like inference call” (2xx completion). so anything that causes 401/403, bad model name, missing env var, etc is high priority.

Marissa Cole: +1. From support pings: users land in Console, create a key, then hit auth errors because they copied the wrong base URL / wrong header. We should make the docs + quickstart snippets idiot-proof.

Paula Mendes: telemetry view: biggest drop-offs are between api_key_created -> first_request_success. error events show a lot of `401_invalid_api_key`, `403_insufficient_scope`, and `model_not_found`.

Logan Wright: can confirm. also seeing malformed JSON bodies for chat completion (missing `messages` array / using `prompt` with the chat endpoint). we probably need a “choose the right endpoint” callout + copy-paste curl.

Jada Williams: what do we think are the top 5 fixes we can land this sprint? I’d propose:
1) One canonical “hello inference” snippet per SDK + curl
2) Env var names consistent across docs/templates (`REDWOOD_API_KEY`, `REDWOOD_BASE_URL`)
3) A “common errors” section that maps error -> fix in 10 seconds
4) Streaming example that’s actually stable (and says when to use it)
5) Make model selection explicit (recommended default + how to list models)

Ethan Wallace: on model selection: we keep saying “pick any model” in marketing copy but in quickstarts we should recommend one default that we know is fast + available. Also link to our benchmark page rather than making claims in-line.

Tyler Benson: quick note: email links + ads will have UTMs. Make sure any “go to console” links don’t 404 / redirect weirdly. We already have a support ticket about wrong console path from an old doc.

Leila Farouk: from QA runs on the starter templates: biggest paper cuts:
- `npm install` works but first run fails because `.env` example missing the base URL (people paste key only)
- curl example uses smart quotes in one place (copy from docs -> breaks)
- python example doesn’t show streaming, but email #3 will push streaming CTA, so we need parity
- errors aren’t actionable: just “Unauthorized” (no hint about header name)

Marissa Cole: for the header issue: some users still send `Authorization: Bearer ...` from other APIs. We should be loud that it’s `x-api-key` (or whatever our SDK expects) and show it in curl.

Logan Wright: yes, and ideally the SDK errors should print “Did you set REDWOOD_API_KEY?” rather than generic stack trace.

Ben Carter: do we have PRs in flight for these already? I saw a couple in GitHub but not sure which are actually landing.

Jada Williams: links:
- Docs update PR (quickstart + troubleshooting + cost dashboard mention): https://github.com/redwood/redwood-docs/pull/622
- Starter template improvements (env vars + better errors): https://github.com/redwood/redwood-quickstarts/pull/311
- TS SDK “hello inference” + first-run errors: https://github.com/redwood/redwood-sdk-typescript/pull/487
- Python SDK README + streaming example: https://github.com/redwood/redwood-sdk-python/pull/512
- Example app “activation recipe” (chat + tracing + cost breakdown): https://github.com/redwood/redwood-examples/pull/209

Redwood Deploy Bot: PR build status update: redwood-docs#622 -> ✅ checks passing (lint + linkcheck)

Allison Grant: from observability side: can we add a line in quickstart that points people to Console -> Latency/Cost dashboard right after first success? That’s one of our “higher-intent milestones” and it reduces the “is this working?” churn.

Henry Cho: yes but keep it “after you get a 2xx” — don’t distract before activation.

Paula Mendes: +1. also, if we can standardize the request IDs in examples (show `x-request-id` output / how to include it in support tickets), Support will love us.

Leila Farouk: can we also add a guardrail note for streaming? we see people confuse “streaming disconnected” with “the API is broken.” maybe a tiny note: “if you’re behind a proxy, try non-streaming first” + link.

Ethan Wallace: careful on claims. we can say “start with non-streaming to validate auth + model selection” without implying infra limitations.

Ben Carter: awesome. I’ll summarize into the Drive doc + tag owners. For sprint scope, let’s prioritize:
- docs#622 + quickstarts#311 for copy/paste reliability + troubleshooting
- TS/Python SDK PRs for hello snippet + better errors
- add a small “model selection + list models” section (if not already)

Jin Woo Park: if you want, I can add a tiny snippet in docs#622 that shows a “list models” call before the first request, but might add friction. maybe better as an optional callout.

Marissa Cole: optional callout sounds right. default model should be in the main path.

Ben Carter: agreed. thanks all. please keep dropping friction bullets + screenshots in the Drive folder. (reactions: Ben Carter added :thumbsup: to Jada Williams’s PR link message)
